purpose: Evaluate evacuation demand, multimodal access, shelter reachability and clearance-time consequences under a declared behavioural and operational model.

mathematical_formulation.capacity: sum_{i,m,p: a in p} f_{i,m,p,t} <= C_{a,t}
mathematical_formulation.clearance: T_clear = min{t: cumulative safe arrivals >= required evacuees}

unlock_rule: Disabled for generic link observations; evacuation demand, safe destinations, capacities and behavioural assumptions must be explicit.

primary_sources.citation: Murray-Tuite and Wolshon (2013), Evacuation transportation modeling: an overview of research, development, and practice, Transportation Research Part C, 27, 25-45.

known_limitations: Normal-day OD demand is not automatically evacuation demand.
Route choice and departure timing require behavioural validation.
Static assignment cannot establish dynamic clearance time.
